newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW - Reaction to Swedish EMU report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Reaction to Swedish EMU report.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the report of Sweden's Calmfors commission on possible Swedish participation in Europe's Economic and Monetary Union.
There is no surprise in the fact that Sweden's entry may be delayed. That was already factored into the market.
For anyone watching the domestic political environement it was fairly obvious that it would be delayed.
It may, hwoever, raise a few eyebrows in other countries where if you meet the Maastricht criteria you are automatically expected to participate in the monetary union.

But Sweden is clearly trying to get through the 1998 election without joining and then I suspect if the Social Deomcrats remain in office we will see a concerted effort to bring people's views around to it.
I can't see Sweden being there for a number of years yet if at all.
I think we may well see a Scandinavian block outside EMU involving Sweden, Norway and Denmark.
The comments are neutral leaning to negative. Personally I have a feeling that the economic discussion has become too dominant, the political apects have come into second place.
No-one benefits from this type of lopsided discussion and I regret that.
If you look at economic factors such as unemployment, the EMU does of course have some bearing, possibly negative. But the EMU perspective is too narrow.

I think (prime minister) Goran Persson and the government will make up their own minds. This is one element of the debate, but is not decisive for what the party leadership and the governent decide in the end. It's ultimately the politicians that have to make their minds up.
